evidence.quote: A) Schematic depicting an example of an at-home HIIT session.

Line plots depicting individual participant heart rate data achieved during the at-home high-intensity interval training (HIIT sessions. The solid line depicts the average heart rate across all completed HIIT sessions, and the grey bands depict the standard deviation. The top dashed line represents the prescribed high-intensity target of 80% heart rate reserve (HRR), the middle-dashed line represents the acceptable high-intensity threshold of 70% HRR, and bottom dashed line represents the recovery target of 30% HRR. Abbreviations: M: Male; F: Female; T: Thoracic; HRR: Heart Rate Reserve.

Line plot depicting the composite high-intensity interval training (HIIT) session data for all participants across all attempted workouts (n=338). Data is normalized to the percent of heart rate reserve (HRR). The solid black line depicts the average heart rate, and the grey bands depict the standard deviation. Dashed lines at 70 and 80% HRR represent acceptable and target HRR for each interval, respectively, and the dashed line at 30% HRR represents the recovery target.

Scatter plot depicting the comparison of age-predicted maximal heart rate versus the measured maximal heart rate during a graded exercise test using arm ergometry. The solid line represents the line of identity and dashed line represents line of best fit. Solid symbols indicate male data and open symbols indicate female data.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

Eight eligible participants completed the trial, presented in Table 1.

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

Participants completed baseline graded exercise tests to determine target heart rate zones.

At-home training sessions were performed using an arm cycle mounted to a wheelchair-accessible hydraulic table (PhysioTrainer UBE and Hydraulic UBE Table, HCI Fitness, Langley, WA, USA). Each in-home unit was provided and installed in the participants’ homes by the study team
Participants were provided with a portable heart rate monitor (Polar H10 Heart Rate Sensor, Polar Electro Inc., Bethpage, NY, USA) that was integrated with a smartphone
After study enrollment, participants underwent an at-home training session to determine HIIT protocol characteristics and ensure proper equipment function/set-up.
Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.
Note that graded exercise tests at baseline, week 8, and week 16 were only available in five participants (P2, P3, P5, P6, P7)
Due to COVID-19 related institutional closures, graded exercise tests performed at baseline, week 8, and week 16 of HIIT were only available in five participants.

Eight eligible participants completed the trial, presented in Table 1.

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

caption_claims.text: Line plots depicting individual participant heart rate data achieved during the at-home high-intensity interval training (HIIT sessions. The solid line depicts the average heart rate across all completed HIIT sessions, and the grey bands depict the standard deviation. The top dashed line represents the prescribed high-intensity target of 80% heart rate reserve (HRR), the middle-dashed line represents the acceptable high-intensity threshold of 70% HRR, and bottom dashed line represents the recovery target of 30% HRR. Abbreviations: M: Male; F: Female; T: Thoracic; HRR: Heart Rate Reserve.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

Eight eligible participants completed the trial, presented in Table 1.

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

evidence.quote: Eight individuals (3 females) with chronic SCI below the sixth thoracic vertebrae participated in a 16-week at-home HIIT program using an arm ergometer.
Eight eligible participants completed the trial

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

At-home training sessions were performed using an arm cycle mounted to a wheelchair-accessible hydraulic table (PhysioTrainer UBE and Hydraulic UBE Table, HCI Fitness, Langley, WA, USA). Each in-home unit was provided and installed in the participants’ homes by the study team
Participants were provided with a portable heart rate monitor (Polar H10 Heart Rate Sensor, Polar Electro Inc., Bethpage, NY, USA) that was integrated with a smartphone
After study enrollment, participants underwent an at-home training session to determine HIIT protocol characteristics and ensure proper equipment function/set-up.
Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

evidence.quote: Eight individuals (3 females) with chronic SCI below the sixth thoracic vertebrae participated in a 16-week at-home HIIT program using an arm ergometer.
Eight eligible participants completed the trial

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

At-home training sessions were performed using an arm cycle mounted to a wheelchair-accessible hydraulic table (PhysioTrainer UBE and Hydraulic UBE Table, HCI Fitness, Langley, WA, USA). Each in-home unit was provided and installed in the participants’ homes by the study team
Participants were provided with a portable heart rate monitor (Polar H10 Heart Rate Sensor, Polar Electro Inc., Bethpage, NY, USA) that was integrated with a smartphone
After study enrollment, participants underwent an at-home training session to determine HIIT protocol characteristics and ensure proper equipment function/set-up.
Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

evidence.quote: Eight individuals (3 females) with chronic SCI below the sixth thoracic vertebrae participated in a 16-week at-home HIIT program using an arm ergometer.
Eight eligible participants completed the trial

Each participant was instructed to complete three at-home HIIT training sessions per week, totaling 48 structured HIIT sessions over 16 weeks. Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

At-home training sessions were performed using an arm cycle mounted to a wheelchair-accessible hydraulic table (PhysioTrainer UBE and Hydraulic UBE Table, HCI Fitness, Langley, WA, USA). Each in-home unit was provided and installed in the participants’ homes by the study team
Participants were provided with a portable heart rate monitor (Polar H10 Heart Rate Sensor, Polar Electro Inc., Bethpage, NY, USA) that was integrated with a smartphone
After study enrollment, participants underwent an at-home training session to determine HIIT protocol characteristics and ensure proper equipment function/set-up.
Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.

Each training session was 24 minutes in length and structured as follows: three-minute warmup, six one-minute high-intensity intervals with a target intensity at 80% of the individuals’ heart rate reserve (HRR, calculated using the Karvonen formula) with two minutes of active recovery, and a three-minute cooldown

At-home training sessions were performed using an arm cycle mounted to a wheelchair-accessible hydraulic table (PhysioTrainer UBE and Hydraulic UBE Table, HCI Fitness, Langley, WA, USA). Each in-home unit was provided and installed in the participants’ homes by the study team
Participants were provided with a portable heart rate monitor (Polar H10 Heart Rate Sensor, Polar Electro Inc., Bethpage, NY, USA) that was integrated with a smartphone
After study enrollment, participants underwent an at-home training session to determine HIIT protocol characteristics and ensure proper equipment function/set-up.
Participants then underwent a supervised training session to ensure correct resistance adjustments and execution of high and low intensity bouts according to heart rate targets.

limitations: Case-series cohort of eight participants; participant-level data come from Tables 1 and 2 only. Table 3, the Mean±SD row, group statistics and adverse-event counts are aggregate and are not copied to individuals.

Adverse events (two shoulder soreness, two tachycardia, one participant missed a week of training) and tachycardia noted by primary care providers before the study are not attributed to any participant in the text; not assigned.
Source statement that all participants were satisfied is cohort-level; Table 2 lists No for P2 Q1 and P8 Q3, and P4 did not complete the survey; no cohort satisfaction was copied to individuals.

Footnote limits some Table 3 data to four participants (P3, P5, P6, P7) because of aberrant gas detections, which by elimination excludes P2 from those rows; no individual Table 3 values are reported, so no measurement fact was assigned.

Eligibility criteria (adult, manual wheelchair use) are stated for participants generally and were not copied to individuals; one withdrawn participant and one excluded participant are not among the eight.

Figure 2 has eight unlabelled subplots titled with sex, level and adherence; six titles match exactly one Table 1 row, the two F - T12 subplots (P1, P2) cannot be told apart. The M - T10 subplot (P7) prints 98% adherance against 100% in Table 1: P7 adherence quarantined as source_conflict with an ambiguity; no panel labels invented.

Figure 1A prints a 5 min cool-down label while the text states a three-minute cooldown and the plotted cool-down segment itself spans 21 to 24 minutes; the schematic is an example, not participant data, so the text prescription is retained and only noted here.
Supplement SD1 ZIP holds a blank SCI Exercise Self-Efficacy Scale form and a STROBE checklist; no patient-level data.

Figure 3 caption gives n=338 attempted workouts while the results text describes an average of 253 training intervals (Table 1 session counts sum to 343); cohort-level counts, not reconciled and not assigned to participants.
Table 1 P6 lists 48 training sessions with 81% adherence, inconsistent with the footnote definition of adherence; both cells quarantined as source_conflict.
SCI ESES self-efficacy scores (three time points) and weekly adverse-event surveys are reported only as cohort statistics; no participant-level values exist, so nothing was assigned.
